human_labels.judge_rationale: The artifact captures the right narrow defect, rerun protocol, isolation, separate judging, and pass-rate reporting. It fails because it does not provide the exact revised instruction with a clear leading directive; it describes how to revise instead of stating the precise replacement text.

observations.value:
Revise the target skill by replacing “make it good” with a concrete, observable completion criterion derived from the skill’s first principles and the case bars. State what outcome must be achieved and which failure smells must be absent. Keep the edit narrowly focused: sharpen the existing criterion before adding any new instructions, and avoid duplicative or no-op language.

Then:

1. Blind-run all three cases again—not only the failed case—using one fresh, context-free agent per case. Each runner receives only its case input and the instruction to use the revised skill.
2. Preserve isolation and sweep the live checkout with `git status` after every run, cleaning any leaked changes.
3. Have separate fresh judges grade each artifact using only the artifact, that case’s bar, and the skill’s first principles. Require evidence-based verdicts for every part of the bar.
4. Re-run important or borderline cases 2–3 times and report pass rates to account for nondeterminism.
5. Continue the revise-and-re-evaluate loop until every case clears its rate bar, or report that the skill structurally cannot express a case rather than forcing a misleading fix.
6. Report the original gap, its mapping to “vague completion criterion,” the exact edit, and before/after pass rates with cited evidence.
